loop.top3_why: The mean combination (B) offers the most stable performance across the three validation windows (all three windows are very close to the overall score) and is less sensitive to the high variance in weight estimation that comes from only three windows. The mean strategy is a robust baseline that is likely to generalize well to the blind test window.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A, while only slightly worse overall, relies on weights derived from a gradient‑boosted meta‑model trained on other series; with only three validation windows the weight estimates are noisy and may not transfer well. Candidate C uses inverse‑error weights on a reduced pool, which can amplify the influence of a few models that happen to perform well in the validation windows but may not be stable across the full horizon. Both A and C therefore carry a higher risk of overfitting compared to the plain mean strategy.
